unresolved_should_improve.claim: The sentence in which Carter interrupts to give telephone orders is removed. 'All traces of displeasure had now left his face' now follows a sentence whose subject is Tommy. Constables also appear at the Soho house with no order having been given.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The earlier frown on Carter lets most readers infer the right referent.

evidence.quote: Half-way through, Mr. Carter interrupted him to give a few cryptic
Half-way through, Mr. Carter interrupted him to give a few cryptic orders through the telephone.
And as briefly as possible he detailed the experiences of the last few days. All traces of displeasure had now left his face.
Two constables were on duty in front of the house in Soho.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's sentence 'Half-way through, Mr. Carter interrupted him to give a few cryptic orders through the telephone.'
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The pronoun briefly points to the wrong man. Carter's urgency, the shift the essentials require from 'annoyed' to 'urgent', loses its visible action.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Carter's telephone orders cut: dangling 'his face' and unmotivated raid

unresolved_should_improve.claim: Three things are cut: Tommy's protest that Annette is not one of the gang, Carter's teasing 'Good-looking, I suppose?', and Tommy's sad inference after the Rita misreading. Carter's judgement goes uncontested, and the misreading no longer costs Tommy anything.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: In 020 Tommy concedes that Annette went back to the gang, so his doubts are short-lived in the source as well.

evidence.quote: I can’t believe she’s really one of them, sir.
The thought saddened him a little, for it seemed to prove that Mrs. Vandemeyer and the girl were on intimate terms.
I can’t believe she’s really one of them, sir. She--seemed so different----
H’m, she must belong to the gang, then; but, being a woman, didn’t feel like standing by to see a personable young man killed.
Dogging ‘Rita’ most likely. By the way, I suppose that’s who Annette meant by Marguerite.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore Tommy's one-line protest. Restore the 'The thought saddened him a little...' sentence after the Rita line.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: planning omission (the essentials list Carter's view but not Tommy's dissent)
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: This flattens the tension between the reader's sympathy for Annette and the evidence against her. That tension carries her clue-laden role and Tommy's emotional stake.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Ambiguity about Annette collapsed into Carter's verdict

unresolved_should_improve.claim: 'Was that a command to him to go? He fancied it was.' and 'She wanted him to go and leave her. But why?' are both cut. Tommy's return to the stairs now follows the triple cry with no interpretation from him.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'He would not go without her' still signals his loyalty.

evidence.quote: Tommy still stood rooted to the ground. Was that a command to him to go?
Tommy had run back to the stairs. She wanted him to go and leave her.
Was that a command to him to go? He fancied it was.
Tommy had run back to the stairs. Then his heart sank.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore 'Was that a command to him to go? He fancied it was.' and 'She wanted him to go and leave her. But why?'
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (essentials: Annette's cry that he has escaped, then the Marguerite cry)
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The cries lose their double function: deception aimed at the gang and a message to Tommy. His choice to go back for her also reads as unmotivated.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Tommy's reading of Annette's cries as a signal to flee removed

unresolved_should_improve.claim: Number 14's 'ordered the carriage' is kept, but the narration identifying the van as that carriage is cut. The van and its driver arrive without explanation.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Attentive readers can connect the van to the carriage themselves.

evidence.quote: In front of the house was a baker’s van. Evidently he was to have been
In front of the house was a baker’s van. Evidently he was to have been taken out of London in that.
We’ve ordered the carriage for your lordship to-morrow mornin’
In front of the house was a baker’s van. The driver jumped to the pavement and tried to bar Tommy’s way.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore 'Evidently he was to have been taken out of London in that.'
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: A planted threat loses its payoff, and the driver's hostility must be guessed.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Baker's van no longer pays off the ordered 'carriage'

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision keeps 'under observation all the time' but drops Tommy's conclusion that he revealed nothing about his identity.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Carter's 'they must have found out about me suddenly' and 020's 'did not know anything about you' still frame the puzzle.

evidence.quote: He had revealed a wish to escape and a desire to find Jane Finn, but nothing that could have given a clue to his own identity.
Had he said anything to give himself away? Hardly.
He saw that he had probably been under observation all the time. Were her denials intended primarily for the listeners?

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore 'Had he said anything to give himself away? Hardly.' and the sentence that follows it.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: Readers may assume the listeners at the peep-hole exposed him. That would quietly answer the puzzle the plan says must stay open, and blunt the later Sunday-timing clue.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Tommy's check that nothing overheard exposed him is cut, blurring the 'twigged' puzzle

unresolved_should_improve.claim: Three spoken lines are cut: her tray excuse, Conrad's 'why did you do that?', and her 'I always turn it out' reply. She now darkens the room silently, and the mockery follows directly.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The plan's verbatim V6 mockery survives, and the light action itself remains.

evidence.quote: I always turn it out. You should have told me.
I always turn it out. You should have told me. Shall I relight it, Monsieur Conrad?
She raised a hand and turned out the light.
“Le beau petit monsieur,” cried Annette, pausing by the bed in the darkness.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore Conrad's 'why did you do that?' and Annette's 'I always turn it out...' reply.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: optional tradeoff, but this cuts beyond the first draft
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: This removes the performed lie that shows her managing Conrad under observation. Tommy's later inference rests on exactly that kind of guarded performance.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Annette's spoken cover for turning out the light removed

unresolved_should_improve.claim: Several of Tommy's set pieces are cut: 'Too late, Tommy remembered his scheme... glad', 'Retire, varlet', the 'economical pleasure' line, and 'Tommy's heart sank'. All were present in the first draft. Only the Pear's soap line and one retort remain.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The plan allows a single Conrad exchange. The revision may also be under target length, which would leave room for restorations; this is unverified.

evidence.quote: “Retire, varlet,” he said, with a wave of his hand.
Too late, Tommy remembered his scheme of obliterating the unprepossessing Conrad.
The door swung open. It was not Conrad who entered, but a girl.
“Talk away,” grunted the man. “It’s little enough time you’ll have to talk in, maybe.”

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the 'Too late... glad' sentences and 'Retire, varlet' from the first draft.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The chapter loses the bravado-versus-fear oscillation that the voice profile names as its comic engine. Tommy reads as a plainer action hero.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Tommy's mock-heroic undercutting stripped
